clue.text: Worn by old lags making a general bolt for it

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the mark rather than a noun synonym

blocks.note: broad as in general or wide-ranging, the 'a' absorbed into the phrase
a bolt is a short arrow fired from a crossbow

explanation.surface: Convicts in old prison garb staging a mass dash for freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: Old lags are long-serving prisoners; British convict uniforms were once stamped with a broad arrow, the government property mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The arrow-shaped government mark was printed all over British prison clothing in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Injured in Yugoslavia

definitions.note: a place description, not a synonym

blocks.note: first meaning: lost blood from a wound
second meaning: a lakeside resort town, now in Slovenia

explanation.surface: Someone hurt while in the Balkans.
explanation.walkthrough: Bled is a lake resort in what was then Yugoslavia, now Slovenia.
explanation.definitionFit: A wounded person loses blood, and the lake town of that name lay in the former Yugoslav republic.

clue.text: Sit on iron work the wrong way round

indicators.note: this says the two pieces are joined in the opposite order to how the clue lists them

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
to iron clothes is to press them

explanation.surface: A careless person sitting on the ironing and creasing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives iron then work; swapped, the work comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit on people figuratively is to suppress or keep them down, which is to oppress them.

clue.text: Where to go for the records of your choice?

definitions.text: Where to go for the records of your choice?

blocks.clueFragment: Where to go for the records of your choice?
blocks.note: surface reading: a shop or library to pick out music
setter's reading: the long-running BBC radio show where guests pick the eight discs they would take when cast away

explanation.surface: Asking which music shop stocks the albums you want.
explanation.walkthrough: Desert Island Discs is a BBC Radio 4 programme in which a guest chooses records to take to an imagined remote isle.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio show's premise sends each castaway guest to an isolated tropical shore with their chosen music.

clue.text: They needed to put one in the net to win

definitions.text: They needed to put one in the net to win

blocks.clueFragment: They needed to put one in the net to win
blocks.note: surface reading: footballers who must score a goal
setter's reading: Roman gladiators who fought by entangling an opponent in a net

explanation.surface: A football team that needs a goal for victory.
explanation.walkthrough: The singular is retiarius, a gladiator armed with a net and trident.
explanation.definitionFit: These arena fighters won by catching their opponent in a weighted net before finishing him off.

clue.text: Bare-headed tramp is at wit's end in the wind

indicators.note: bare-headed means without a head, so the opening letter is lost
an end is the final letter of the word wit's

blocks.note: a hobo is a tramp
taken as written
the last letter of wit

explanation.surface: A homeless man, out of ideas, standing hatless in the breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: HOBO loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboe player sits in the woodwind section of an orchestra, so is one in the wind.

clue.text: Grouse meat

blocks.note: first meaning: a complaint, a gripe
second meaning: flesh from cattle

explanation.walkthrough: Grouse reads as the game bird, which makes 'meat' look like a description of it; here it is a grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a complaint in informal speech and the flesh of cows sold by butchers.

clue.text: English church in want of both sexes

indicators.note: in places the church abbreviation inside the word for want

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for English
to pine is to long or want
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: An English church short of both men and women.
explanation.definitionFit: Epicene means having the characteristics of both male and female, or neither, androgynous.

clue.text: A firm boundary perhaps past point

blocks.note: in cricket a boundary hit along the ground scores four runs
point is a fielding position, and a shot past it goes square of the wicket

explanation.surface: A company's office line lying beyond a given spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket again: a four is a boundary, and square is the zone level with the batsman where point fields.
explanation.definitionFit: Foursquare means solidly based and steady, unwavering in stance or support.

clue.text: A fair account

blocks.note: first meaning: a large public exhibition or show
second meaning: a detailed explanation or description

explanation.walkthrough: 'A fair account' reads as an honest report; split it into a show and a description.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is both a trade exhibition held for the public and a thorough setting-out of ideas.

clue.text: Helpful sort of tenant's place

blocks.note: surface reading: an obliging kind of lodger
setter's reading: a deputy officer's title, whose first part stands before the word tenant

explanation.surface: A cooperative lodger's home.
explanation.walkthrough: A lieutenant is a helper or deputy; take away 'tenant' and the place that is left is LIEU, which itself means place, as in 'in lieu of'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieu is a French-derived word for stead or position, surviving in the English phrase in lieu of.

clue.text: A brilliant Peruvian generation

blocks.note: Incan describes the Inca people of ancient Peru
descent is lineage, the line of generations

explanation.surface: Praising a talented young age group from Peru.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent means glowing white-hot, so dazzlingly bright, and figuratively outstanding.

clue.text: Tail-end hold up

blocks.note: first meaning: the back part
second meaning: raise, lift upright

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hold up' suggests a delay at the back of a queue; here it means to raise, as a horse rears.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word is the back portion; as a verb it means to lift or bring up children.

clue.text: Wild beast seen — these children aren't going to school

definitions.text: these children aren't going to school

indicators.note: wild means untamed and disordered, so the following letters run loose into another order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Truanting children spotted running riot like an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Absentees are people missing from where they should be, here pupils skipping school lessons.

clue.text: A religious qualification is a double degree in Africa

definitions.note: a place description rather than a noun

blocks.note: taken as written
DD is Doctor of Divinity
taken as written
A plus BA twice, a Bachelor of Arts doubled

explanation.surface: Remarks on an academic holding several qualifications somewhere in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Addis Ababa is the capital city of Ethiopia in the Horn of the continent.

clue.text: It takes a woman with courage to water down resolution

blocks.note: Di is a short woman's name, Diana
spirit means courage or mettle; 'with' joins it on

explanation.surface: Only a bold woman can weaken someone's determination.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispirit is to sap someone's morale, weakening their determination and resolve.

clue.text: A casual shirt worn by boy friend in boat

indicators.note: something worn is put on and surrounded by the wearer, so one piece sits inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
a T-shirt is the casual shirt, shortened to its letter
a beau is a boyfriend

explanation.surface: A girl's boyfriend lounging in a T-shirt aboard a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A and T go inside BEAU after its B, giving B-AT-EAU, the French word for boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Bateau is French for boat and names a flat-bottomed river craft in English usage.

clue.text: Blunt lie slipped into official report

indicators.note: something that has slipped has moved out of place, so these letters shift into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An outright falsehood sneaked into a government statement.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official statement or news announcement issued to the public.

clue.text: It's fashionable and healthy to drag on a fag

blocks.note: in means trendy
hale means robust, as in hale and hearty

explanation.surface: An ironic claim that smoking is trendy and good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a fag is a cigarette, and a drag is a puff on one.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking a drag on a cigarette means drawing its smoke into the lungs, which is breathing in.

clue.text: Kneeler with hose

blocks.note: to have something is to be with it
hose are stockings, and a sock is one

explanation.surface: Someone kneeling in stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: A hassock is the padded cushion knelt on in a church pew.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassock is a firm cushion for kneeling on during prayers in church.

clue.text: Beat a retreat before the king's hit man appears

indicators.note: in retreat a thing goes backwards, so the word for beat is read from its end

blocks.note: to drum is to beat rhythmically
ere is an old word for before
R stands for rex, king

explanation.surface: A soldier's drumbeat sounding the retreat before the king's assassin shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat a retreat' is a stock phrase for withdrawing, but here the beat itself retreats, and the 's of 'king's' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit man is a contract killer, so he is one who commits murder.

clue.text: Information from a computer about a reported suspect

indicators.note: reported means passed on in speech, so the word for suspect is taken by its sound

blocks.note: re means concerning
taken as written
to suspect is to doubt, whose B is silent

explanation.surface: Computer data concerning a suspect named in a police report.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubt is pronounced without its B, so it is spelt as it sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A readout is the displayed or printed output of data produced by a computer or instrument.

clue.text: Bark, making a harsh sound

blocks.note: first meaning: graze the skin, as a barked shin
second meaning: a grating noise

explanation.walkthrough: Bark suggests a dog; here it means to graze, as in barking your knee.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape is to graze skin by rubbing, and a scrape is the rasping noise of that rubbing.

clue.text: In charge, in a munitions factory, of the poison

indicators.note: in places one piece within another, here inside the factory word

blocks.note: an arsenal is where weapons and ammunition are made or stored
IC is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: The person running a weapons plant handles toxic materials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of the poison' is an adjectival definition: the answer describes something relating to arsenic.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenical is the adjective for things containing or relating to arsenic, a classic poison.

clue.text: Strikes back in petty quarrel

indicators.note: back says the word for strikes is read from right to left

blocks.note: taps are light blows

explanation.surface: Hitting back during a trivial row.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a brief, minor argument over something trivial, a tiff.

clue.text: He supplies cues and is paid

blocks.note: first meaning: a comedian's straight man who sets up the jokes
second meaning

explanation.surface: An actor prompting lines and getting wages.
explanation.walkthrough: A feed is the stooge who gives a comic the lines to answer; the second half playfully reads it as fee'd.
explanation.definitionFit: In comedy a feed is the partner delivering lines for the comedian's punchline, and fee'd jokily means remunerated.

clue.text: Call for a small vessel

blocks.note: taken as written
a hoy is a small coasting vessel

explanation.surface: A sailor's shout to hail a little boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads naturally as a definition of the call itself, which is what makes it neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahoy is the traditional nautical shout used to hail a ship or attract attention.

clue.text: War artist's racket

blocks.note: a battle is fighting in war
Gustave Doré, the French illustrator; the 's just joins

explanation.surface: A painter's swindle connected with warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' looks like a scam; it is the bat used in the old game of battledore and shuttlecock.
explanation.definitionFit: A battledore is a small paddle-shaped bat, an early form of badminton racquet.

clue.text: Tau cross carried by Tutankhamen

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the letters sit within the pharaoh's name

blocks.note: the letters run consecutively inside this name

explanation.surface: The boy pharaoh bearing an Egyptian symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the Egyptian symbol is held inside the Egyptian king's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The ankh is the looped tau cross, the Egyptian symbol of life often shown held by pharaohs.

clue.text: Sappers, batting, declared and got put back in

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are sappers
a batsman at the crease is in
stated means said or declared

explanation.surface: Army engineers at a cricket match, batting, declaring their innings and being sent back in.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a team that declares ends its innings voluntarily, which makes 'put back in' look like more cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To be reinstated is to be restored to a former position, office or place.
